newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bitter Bosnian soldiers halt traffic in Tuzla.
newsitem.headline: Bitter Bosnian soldiers halt traffic in Tuzla.

text.p: Hundreds of demobilised Bosnian soldiers, some on crutches, halted traffic on the outskirts of Tuzla on Monday to press for more post-war government benefits.
The protesters blocked the main road between Sarajevo and Tuzla and the northern border crossing with Croatia, a Reuters reporter said.
He said mile-long columns of vehicles, including heavy trucks, were parked on the roads outside Moslem-controlled Tuzla, the second largest city in territory under government control.
"There are a lot of unresolved problems with demobilised soldiers, first of all their status and medical treatment," said one of the protesters, Enver Kantic, 26.
He said the protesters would spend the night on the road and persist in the stoppage until their demands were resolved.
"Unfortunately, there seems to be no other way to fight for our rights," another demobilised soldier told Reuters.
The 43-month Bosnian war halted in December 1995, with a peace treaty dividing the country in the Croat-Moslem federation and the Serb entity, linked by a loose central government body.
Faced with growing demands for money and social benefits the federal government has opened savings accounts with thousands of German mark deposits for all demobilised soldiers.
But the account remains effectively unusable, as the beneficiaries are not allowed to withdraw cash from it.
"Those in power find apartments for themselves and throw former soliders out," a protester said. "They buy companies while we are starving."
